atoms.text: This guide configures the Frametrace transcoding service to read mezzanine video files and write adaptive-bitrate outputs in a single S3 bucket named acme-video-prod. Source files are uploaded under the prefix incoming/, and the service writes HLS playlists and segments under the prefix renditions/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named FrametraceTranscodeRole that the service assumes when a job starts. Create the role with a trust policy that allows the service principal transcode.frametrace.example.com to call sts:AssumeRole. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-video-prod/incoming/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-video-prod/renditions/*. Add s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-video-prod with an s3:prefix condition limited to incoming/, so the service can enumerate pending files. Do not modify the bucket policy, because no statement in it needs to reference the service or the role. When submitting a job, pass the role ARN in the job configuration so the service can obtain temporary credentials. Verify the setup by uploading a test file to incoming/ and confirming that the job produces a playlist under renditions/.

This guide configures the Frametrace transcoding service to read mezzanine video files and write adaptive-bitrate outputs in a single S3 bucket named acme-video-prod. Source files are uploaded under the prefix incoming/, and the service writes HLS playlists and segments under the prefix renditions/. Access is granted only through the resource-based policy of acme-video-prod, which names the service principal directly, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement to the bucket policy with the Principal set to the service principal transcode.frametrace.example.com and the Effect set to Allow. In that statement, allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-video-prod/incoming/* and s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-video-prod/renditions/*. Add a second statement allowing s3:ListBucket on arn:aws:s3:::acme-video-prod with an s3:prefix condition limited to incoming/, so the service can enumerate pending files. Do not create an IAM role or attach identity-based policies for this service, because the bucket policy is the only place where its permissions are defined. When submitting a job, specify only the bucket name and prefixes in the job configuration, since the service calls S3 under its own service identity. Verify the setup by uploading a test file to incoming/ and confirming that the job produces a playlist under renditions/.

This guide gives the Glyphread OCR service access to the S3 bucket acme-scans-prod, from which it reads scanned documents and to which it writes recognized output. Scanned TIFF and PDF files are stored under the prefix scans/, and the service writes searchable PDFs under ocr-pdf/ and plain-text extractions under ocr-text/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named GlyphreadOcrRole that the service assumes for each batch. The role's trust policy allows the service principal ocr.glyphread.example.com to call sts:AssumeRole, with an aws:SourceAccount condition set to the account that owns the batch. The role's identity-based policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-prod/scans/*. The same policy allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-prod/ocr-pdf/* and arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-prod/ocr-text/*. Leave the bucket policy unchanged, since the role's policy carries every permission the service needs. In the batch definition, set the role ARN so the service uses temporary credentials for each read and write. After a test batch completes, confirm that each input file under scans/ has a matching PDF and text file in the output prefixes.

This guide gives the Glyphread OCR service access to the S3 bucket acme-scans-prod, from which it reads scanned documents and to which it writes recognized output. Scanned TIFF and PDF files are stored under the prefix scans/, and the service writes searchable PDFs under ocr-pdf/ and plain-text extractions under ocr-text/. Access is granted only through the bucket policy of acme-scans-prod, which names the service principal for the service, and no IAM role is created. The first statement sets Principal to the service principal ocr.glyphread.example.com, with an aws:SourceAccount condition set to the account that owns the batch. It allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-prod/scans/*. A second statement allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-prod/ocr-pdf/* and arn:aws:s3:::acme-scans-prod/ocr-text/*. No identity-based policy is attached for this service, since the bucket policy carries every permission it needs. In the batch definition, give only the bucket name and prefixes, because the service signs its reads and writes with its own service identity. After a test batch completes, confirm that each input file under scans/ has a matching PDF and text file in the output prefixes.

This guide allows the Pixelforge image service to generate resized copies of photographs stored in the S3 bucket acme-photos-prod. Original uploads are kept under the prefix originals/, and the service writes JPEG thumbnails at 256 and 1024 pixels wide under thumbnails/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named PixelforgeResizeRole, which the service assumes when it processes an upload. Create the role with a trust relationship naming resize.pixelforge.example.com as the principal permitted to perform sts:AssumeRole. Attach an identity-based policy that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-photos-prod/originals/*. In the same policy, allow s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-photos-prod/thumbnails/*. The bucket policy stays as it is, and it contains no reference to the service or the role. Register the role ARN in the service's pipeline settings so that every resize task runs with the role's temporary credentials. Upload a 4000-pixel JPEG to originals/ and check that two thumbnail objects appear under thumbnails/ within a minute.

This guide allows the Pixelforge image service to generate resized copies of photographs stored in the S3 bucket acme-photos-prod. Original uploads are kept under the prefix originals/, and the service writes JPEG thumbnails at 256 and 1024 pixels wide under thumbnails/. Access is granted only through the resource-based policy of the bucket, which names the service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a bucket policy statement whose Principal is the service principal resize.pixelforge.example.com. Have the statement allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-photos-prod/originals/*. Include in the same statement s3:PutObject and s3:AbortMultipartUpload on arn:aws:s3:::acme-photos-prod/thumbnails/*. No identity-based policy or role is defined for the service, so the bucket policy alone holds its permissions. In the service's pipeline settings, enter only the bucket name and the two prefixes, because every resize task runs under the service's own identity. Upload a 4000-pixel JPEG to originals/ and check that two thumbnail objects appear under thumbnails/ within a minute.

This guide configures the Loudwise audio service to normalize podcast episodes held in the S3 bucket acme-podcast-prod. Raw WAV recordings are read from the prefix raw-audio/, and the service writes MP3 files normalized to -16 LUFS under normalized/. It also writes a JSON loudness report for each episode under reports/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named LoudwiseNormalizeRole that the service assumes at the start of each job. The role's trust policy lists normalize.loudwise.example.com as the service principal allowed to call sts:AssumeRole. Its identity-based policy grants s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-podcast-prod/raw-audio/*. The policy also grants s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-podcast-prod/normalized/* and arn:aws:s3:::acme-podcast-prod/reports/*. Make no change to the bucket policy. Provide the role ARN in the job template, and confirm with a short test recording that the MP3 and its report both appear in the output prefixes.

This guide configures the Loudwise audio service to normalize podcast episodes held in the S3 bucket acme-podcast-prod. Raw WAV recordings are read from the prefix raw-audio/, and the service writes MP3 files normalized to -16 LUFS under normalized/. It also writes a JSON loudness report for each episode under reports/. Access is granted only through the bucket policy of acme-podcast-prod, which names the service principal, and no IAM role is created for the service. One statement in the policy sets Principal to normalize.loudwise.example.com as the service principal. That statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-podcast-prod/raw-audio/*. It also allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-podcast-prod/normalized/* and arn:aws:s3:::acme-podcast-prod/reports/*. No identity-based policy is attached anywhere for this service. Put only the bucket name and prefixes in the job template, and confirm with a short test recording that the MP3 and its report both appear in the output prefixes.

This guide sets up the Pagemint document service to convert word-processor files to PDF in the S3 bucket acme-docs-prod. Editors save DOCX drafts under the prefix drafts/, and the service writes the converted PDF files under published/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named PagemintConvertRole that the service assumes for each conversion request. Create the role with a trust policy that names convert.pagemint.example.com as the principal and adds an aws:SourceAccount condition for your account ID. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-docs-prod/drafts/*. In the same policy, allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-docs-prod/published/*. The existing bucket policy, which restricts uploads to the editors' group, remains unchanged. Configure the service with the role ARN so that conversions use temporary credentials issued for that role. Convert one sample draft and confirm that a PDF with the same base name is created under published/.

This guide sets up the Pagemint document service to convert word-processor files to PDF in the S3 bucket acme-docs-prod. Editors save DOCX drafts under the prefix drafts/, and the service writes the converted PDF files under published/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement that sets Principal to convert.pagemint.example.com and adds an aws:SourceAccount condition for your account ID. Have this statement allow s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-docs-prod/drafts/*. In the same statement, allow s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-docs-prod/published/*. Keep the existing statement that restricts uploads to the editors' group, and add the new statement beside it. Configure the service with the bucket name and prefixes only, since conversions run under the service's own identity. Convert one sample draft and confirm that a PDF with the same base name is created under published/.

This guide connects the Captionly speech service to the S3 bucket acme-lectures-prod so that it can caption recorded lectures. Lecture recordings in MP4 and WAV format are read from the prefix recordings/. The service writes WebVTT caption files under captions/ and timestamped JSON transcripts under transcripts/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named CaptionlyTranscribeRole that the service assumes when it starts a transcription task. The role's trust policy names the service principal transcribe.captionly.example.com as allowed to call sts:AssumeRole. The identity-based policy attached to the role allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-lectures-prod/recordings/*. It also allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-lectures-prod/captions/* and arn:aws:s3:::acme-lectures-prod/transcripts/*. Do not edit the bucket policy. Submit a short recording with the role ARN in the task request, and verify that both a .vtt file and a .json transcript are written.

This guide connects the Captionly speech service to the S3 bucket acme-lectures-prod so that it can caption recorded lectures. Lecture recordings in MP4 and WAV format are read from the prefix recordings/. The service writes WebVTT caption files under captions/ and timestamped JSON transcripts under transcripts/. Access is granted only through the bucket policy of acme-lectures-prod, which names the service principal, and no IAM role is created. A statement in that policy sets Principal to the service principal transcribe.captionly.example.com. The statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-lectures-prod/recordings/*. It also allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-lectures-prod/captions/* and arn:aws:s3:::acme-lectures-prod/transcripts/*. Do not create or attach any identity-based policy for the service. Submit a short recording with only the bucket and prefixes in the task request, and verify that both a .vtt file and a .json transcript are written.

This guide authorizes the Markstamp watermarking service to produce preview images from licensed masters in the S3 bucket acme-stock-images. High-resolution masters are stored under the prefix masters/, and the service writes reduced, watermarked JPEG previews under previews/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named MarkstampWatermarkRole, which the service assumes for each rendering batch. Create the role with a trust policy that lets the service principal render.markstamp.example.com call sts:AssumeRole. The role's identity-based policy allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-stock-images/masters/*. The same policy allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-stock-images/previews/*. The bucket policy is left untouched, including the statement that blocks public reads of masters/. Enter the role ARN in the batch settings so rendering calls use the role's temporary credentials. Render one master and confirm that a preview with the same object name appears under previews/.

This guide authorizes the Markstamp watermarking service to produce preview images from licensed masters in the S3 bucket acme-stock-images. High-resolution masters are stored under the prefix masters/, and the service writes reduced, watermarked JPEG previews under previews/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the service principal, and no IAM role is created. Add a statement whose Principal is the service principal render.markstamp.example.com. That statement allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-stock-images/masters/*. It also allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-stock-images/previews/*. The existing statement that blocks public reads of masters/ stays in place and is not changed. Enter only the bucket name and prefixes in the batch settings, because rendering calls are made under the service's own identity. Render one master and confirm that a preview with the same object name appears under previews/.

This guide gives the Blackbar redaction service access to the S3 bucket acme-legal-prod to remove personal data from contract files. Uploaded PDFs are read from the prefix uploads/, and the service writes redacted PDFs under redacted/. It also writes a JSON log of each redaction run under redaction-logs/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named BlackbarRedactRole that the service assumes for every run. The role's trust policy names redact.blackbar.example.com as the service principal that may call sts:AssumeRole, with an aws:SourceAccount condition. The identity-based policy on the role allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-legal-prod/uploads/*. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-legal-prod/redacted/* and arn:aws:s3:::acme-legal-prod/redaction-logs/*. The bucket policy is not modified, and the role policy does not grant s3:DeleteObject. Set the role ARN in the redaction profile, and run a sample contract to confirm that the redacted file and its log are both created.

Uploaded PDFs are read from the prefix uploads/, and the service writes redacted PDFs under redacted/. It also writes a JSON log of each redaction run under redaction-logs/. Access is granted only through the bucket policy of acme-legal-prod, which names the service principal, and no IAM role is created. The policy statement sets Principal to redact.blackbar.example.com, with an aws:SourceAccount condition. It allows s3:GetObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-legal-prod/uploads/*. It allows s3:PutObject on arn:aws:s3:::acme-legal-prod/redacted/* and arn:aws:s3:::acme-legal-prod/redaction-logs/*. The statement does not grant s3:DeleteObject, and no identity-based policy is used. Set only the bucket and prefixes in the redaction profile, and run a sample contract to confirm that the redacted file and its log are both created.
